newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin unfazed by Belarus, sees conflict ending.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin unfazed by Belarus, sees conflict ending.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin is sticking to his view that the political crisis in Belarus is being defused after Russian intervention and sees no need to rush Moscow's diplomacy, his spokesman said on Saturday.

Sergei Yastrzhembsky said Yeltsin considered Friday's Moscow-brokered compromise as the first key step in ending the conflict, despite its apparent failure. "Boris Nikolayevich (Yeltsin) consdiders there is no need to jump to conclusions. He very much counts on the process of fulfilling the agreement being continued and brought to a conclusion."
Yastrzhembsky, addressing a regular news briefing, said Yeltsin had received reports on Saturday morning at the Barvikha sanatorium near Moscow where he is convalescing from heart surgery.

The president, who called Friday's deal "a great victory" for Russian diplomacy, still believed it had achieved a sharp reduction in tension and that it was natural that it had met some resistance in parliament.

"You should understand the president's statement as saying there is a sharp drop in tension, that the worst of the crisis is over," Yastrzhembsky said. "But that does not mean that the crisis itself has already been happily settled."
